name: IRCTC (Indian Railway Catering & Tourism Corporation)
tagline: Genuine government-granted monopoly (e-ticketing convenience fee, Rail Neer, catering, rail tourism) — high ROE, debt-free, but a ~Rs 38,000 Cr large-cap compounding in the low-to-mid teens, with no named inflection to lift it to the 10x/100x bar
business_overview: IRCTC is the exclusive Indian Railways arm for online passenger ticketing (earning a per-ticket convenience fee), packaged drinking water (Rail Neer), on-board and static catering, and rail-based tourism (Bharat Gaurav trains, Tejas, luxury tourism). The internet-ticketing segment is the profit engine — near-zero capital, monopoly pricing on the convenience fee. Government of India holds ~62%.
fundamentals_table: ~11% (FY26 revenue from operations ~Rs 5,215 Cr, all-time high)
fundamentals_narrative: Best-in-class return profile (ROE ~37%, negligible debt, ~49% payout) on a monopoly franchise. But growth is structurally moderate — FY26 revenue up ~11% to a record ~Rs 5,215 Cr — and the two biggest swing factors (the convenience-fee rate and any move to share it with the government) are political/regulatory, not management-controlled. Catering and tourism are lower-margin and operationally heavier. At ~Rs 38,000 Cr the stock trades on a rich multiple for a low-to-mid-teens grower.

Long structural runway for digitised travel, rail modernisation, and premium rail tourism as discretionary spend rises

Segment mix dilutes quality: catering and tourism are lower-margin and more execution-intensive than the ticketing core
Valuation is full for the growth rate; re-rating room is limited
